end.summary:
Tara practised distinguishing observations, hypotheses, laws and theories using dog behaviour and boiling-point examples.
They identified observations and testable hypotheses across three unaided attempts each.
Tara mixed up the scientific meaning of theory with the idea that theories become laws after proof.
This mix-up remained at the end; the final sequence still placed theory after repeated testing.
end.parentNote: Tara practised sorting observations, hypotheses, laws and theories, and used checking with a thermometer as an example of testing. Tara explained observations and hypotheses with a clear step-by-step method, but continued to say that a proven theory becomes a law; this was not corrected by the end of the lesson. At home, ask Tara to make two columns—“theory” and “law”—and write that both are well-supported scientific ideas with different roles, not stages of a ladder.
